reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because the spoken presentation and visible demonstrations are primarily an educational tutorial on using Coinbase to buy, sell, transfer, and secure cryptocurrency. The description includes referral links and instructions mentioning Bitconnect, including sending Bitcoin to purchase BCC and make a loan, but it does not provide a concrete deceptive return claim or establish that the creator is misrepresenting the destination. The available evidence therefore supports a Coinbase tutorial with promotional elements rather than a confirmed deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: in today's video I'm going over an in-depth tutorial on how to buy and sell cryptocurrency on the coinbase app, how to set up and security features and how to navigate the overall Coinbase exchange on both their app and website
If you found the video helpful and would like to join Coinbase and give it a try, I put my referral link down in the description box.

if you invite a friend and they join Coinbase to your referral link, if they purchase $100 worth of digital currency cryptocurrency within the first 180 days, both they and you will receive $10 worth of free Bitcoin to your Coinbase account
watch step by step video on how to send bitcoins to bitconnect backoffice and then buy bcc and do your first loan
So you definitely want to go into Security under the settings tab, verify your phone and setup the Google Authenticator app or Authy App to get that level of security.

opening.argument: The video links a concrete cryptocurrency reward to a recruitment-and-purchase sequence. Viewers are told to invite a friend through the speaker's referral link, have that person purchase digital currency, and receive free Bitcoin. The accompanying screen reinforces the same inducement with “INVITE FRIENDS AND GET FREE BITCOIN,” while the description supplies external cryptocurrency links and directs viewers toward further participation. This is more than neutral platform instruction: the requested actions are explicitly tied to an asset reward, making the solicitation itself the central scam signal.

Step 1 : Join Here https://bitconnect.co/?ref=Iamphresh

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the presentation a tutorial does not answer the specific reward solicitation. The speaker expressly asks viewers to use the referral link and conditions the free Bitcoin on another person's purchase. The presence of interface demonstrations cannot erase that linked action-and-reward mechanism, and the description goes beyond Coinbase navigation by directing viewers toward Bitconnect participation.

watch step by step video on how to send bitcoins to bitconnect backoffice and then buy bcc and do your first loan

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The reward is a disclosed, ordinary referral incentive, not proof of deception: the evidence only says both participants receive $10 after a stated purchase condition. The spoken purpose remains instruction about Coinbase operations, including buying, selling, transferring, and security. Nothing here shows that the referral reward was fake, concealed, or connected to a fraudulent outcome.

opening.argument: Several concrete risk signals appear together: cryptocurrency transfers, external destinations, a token purchase, a loan instruction, and an easy “free Bitcoin” incentive. The description tells viewers to send Bitcoin to a Bitconnect back office and then “buy bcc and do your first loan,” while the referral page ties inviting others and a qualifying purchase to free Bitcoin. Even without an explicit guaranteed-profit sentence, this combination creates a direct pathway from viewer action and funds to promised digital-asset rewards, with the external-link and lending language making the solicitation materially riskier than ordinary education.

Step 1 : Join Here https://bitconnect.co/?ref=Iamphresh

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense isolates the Coinbase interface and treats each signal as harmless in isolation. But the relevant evidence is the combination: an external Bitconnect link, instructions to transfer Bitcoin and enter a loan, and a reward tied to recruiting a purchaser. The lack of a guaranteed-return phrase does not make this money-flow solicitation benign; it simply means the risk is expressed through actions and incentives rather than a headline promise.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited material establishes crypto-related actions and a referral reward, but not deception, guaranteed returns, or a harmful outcome. The Bitconnect instruction appears in the description, while the supplied spoken material focuses on Coinbase navigation and security. Risky subject matter and external links can warrant caution, but they do not by themselves prove that the reward or service was fraudulent.

opening.argument: Although presented as a Coinbase tutorial, the content functions as promotion: viewers are encouraged to join through a referral link, invite friends, and direct another person's qualifying purchase, while the screen visibly provides invite and sharing controls. The description also markets several external services and tells viewers to follow the creator on social media. This promotional role matters because the educational walkthrough supplies credibility for a participation funnel, and the referral reward depends on recruiting another user into a funded cryptocurrency transaction. The tutorial framing therefore does not make the solicitation ordinary or neutral.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that the speaker teaches Coinbase features does not negate the promotional function. He explicitly invites viewers to join through his link, and the referral page turns social sharing into a path toward free Bitcoin. The interface lesson can be the vehicle that makes the solicitation appear trustworthy; it is not evidence that no recruitment commission or promotional steering occurred.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion does not equal a recruitment scheme or deception. The evidence shows a disclosed one-level referral incentive tied to a specific purchase, not downlines, tiers, matrices, or hidden commissions. The main presentation repeatedly describes and demonstrates Coinbase functions, including buying, selling, transfers, and account security; the referral invitation is an ancillary promotional element.
